skill.name: design-to-code
skill.description: Convert Figma designs into React and TypeScript components with coderio. The workflow creates design protocols, extracts props, and saves generated UI files.
skill.summary: Convert Figma designs into React components using a guided coderio workflow.
skill.author: MigoXLab

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown fences, JavaScript template literals, and expected local workflow files. The remaining risks are limited to unvalidated local path inputs, generated code writes, and Figma token handling through an external helper.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated component names can influence props file reads.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict component names to safe filename characters and reject path separators before reading props files.

remediation.issue: Generated protocol paths influence where code is saved.
remediation.suggestion: Normalize resolved paths and enforce that generated files remain under the intended src component directory.

remediation.issue: Figma tokens are passed to an external helper dependency.
remediation.suggestion: Document token handling, avoid logging tokens, and pin dependency versions used by the helper script.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Figma Token Passed To External Helper
semantic_findings.description: The workflow asks users to provide a Figma token, then passes it into an imported coderio helper. The visible code does not show token handling inside that dependency.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The token flow is explicit in the documentation and script. There is no proof of exfiltration, but the token leaves local code boundaries through an external helper.

semantic_findings.title: Generated Protocol Paths Drive Project Writes
semantic_findings.description: The save-code command reads component paths from protocol data and writes generated code into the project. The visible code does not validate the resolved output path.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The write path depends on protocol data generated earlier in the workflow. The helper may normalize paths, but this file does not show an explicit containment check.

content.value_statement: Design handoff often loses layout details and component structure. This skill guides Figma to React conversion with repeatable prompts and helper scripts.
actual_capabilities: Fetches Figma design data and a thumbnail using the helper script.
Creates prompts for structure, props, and React component generation.
Stores workflow artifacts in process and scripts directories.
Builds component task lists from the generated design protocol.
Saves generated React and TypeScript component files into the project.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or later and a Figma personal access token.
Depends on the coderio package and network access to Figma.
Requires users to attach thumbnails and save AI outputs between steps.
Does not automatically prove browser visual parity after generation.

use_cases.title: Build From A Figma Frame
use_cases.description: Convert a selected Figma frame into a React project with generated components and assets.

use_cases.title: Prepare Design Handoff
use_cases.description: Turn visual structure, repeated components, and props into implementation-ready tasks.

use_cases.title: Accelerate Prototype Implementation
use_cases.description: Create a working Vite and Tailwind CSS interface from an approved visual design.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Frame
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a single Figma frame.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-to-code to convert my Figma frame into React and TypeScript. Follow the workflow and tell me which files need review.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Component Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the generated thumbnail and protocol to extract props for each repeated component. Keep labels, image paths, and order exact.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Ordered Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the React components in task order. Save each result through the helper workflow and keep parent imports consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Review And Integrate Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the generated components for visual fidelity, unsafe paths, and missing assets. Then integrate the root component into the app.

output_examples.input: A landing page frame with hero content, feature sections, and a footer.
output_examples.output: A structured React implementation plan with generated components, assets, and integration guidance.

output_examples.input: A dashboard design with repeated cards, charts, and navigation.
output: Component groups identified from the design.
Props extracted for repeated UI patterns.
Ordered generation tasks for leaf and parent components.

output_examples.input: A mobile app screen with icons, imagery, and repeated list items.
output_examples.output: Generated component tasks that preserve text content, image references, and layout hierarchy.

best_practices: Use a scoped Figma token and remove it from shell history after use.
Review every generated file before committing or running the application.
Keep generated artifacts in the documented process and scripts directories.
anti_patterns: Do not paste unrelated secrets into prompts or generated workflow files.
Do not skip visual review after generating components.
Do not run helper commands from an unexpected working directory.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It guides generation of React and TypeScript components from Figma design data and thumbnails.

faq.question: Does it need a Figma token?
faq.answer: Yes. The fetch step requires a Figma personal access token with access to the target file.

faq.question: Can it work without network access?
faq.answer: No. The Figma fetch step and dependency installation require network access.

faq.question: Does it automatically create perfect code?
faq.answer: No. It creates a guided workflow, but users must review generated code and visual fidelity.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Where are intermediate files stored?
faq.answer: The helper uses local process and scripts directories for thumbnails, protocols, prompts, and task files.
